title: Person-Specific Statistics and Heterogeneous Dynamic Networks
code: library(idiographic)  ## simulate an ESM panel: 30 people, 40 occasions, 3 predictors set.seed(1) panel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:30, function(id) {   x <- matrix(rnorm(120), 40, 3)   data.frame(id = id, time = 1:40, A = x[, 1], B = x[, 2], C = x[, 3]) })) panel$Y <- 0.7 * panel$A - 0.3 * panel$B +   rep(rnorm(30, sd = 0.5), each = 40) + rnorm(nrow(panel), sd = 0.4)  ## 1. inspect variation and dependence person by person describe_persons(panel, id = "id", vars = c("A", "B", "Y"), time = "time") correlate_persons(panel, id = "id", vars = c("A", "B", "Y")) variance_components(panel, id = "id", vars = c("A", "B", "Y"))  ## 2. prepare within-person predictors and honest lags prepared <- preprocess_panel(   panel, id = "id", time = "time", vars = c("A", "B"),   decompose = TRUE, lag = 1 )  ## 3. compare pooled and person-specific regression on later observations reg <- fit_lm(prepared, y = "Y", x = c("A", "B"), id = "id",               time = "time", scope = "both") metrics(reg, overall = TRUE) coefs(reg, scope = "individual")  ## 4. separate within-person and between-person effects directly wb <- fit_within_between(panel, y = "Y", x = c("A", "B"), id = "id",                          time = "time") contextual(wb)  ## 5. stabilize noisy individual coefficients pool_coefs(reg) shrink_coefs(reg)  ## 6. fit and tune scoped machine-learning models ml <- fit_ml(panel, y = "Y", x = c("A", "B", "C"), id = "id",              time = "time", scope = "both",              model = c("ridge", "knn"), tune = TRUE) best_model(ml) predictions(ml, scope = "individual")

code: # \donttest{ # Create simple panel data (3 subjects, 4 variables, 50 time points). set.seed(42) n_sub <- 3; n_t <- 50; vars <- paste0("V", 1:4) rows <- lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {   d <- as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(n_t * 4), ncol = 4))   names(d) <- vars; d$id <- i; d }) panel <- do.call(rbind, rows) res <- fit_gimme(panel, vars = vars, id = "id") print(res) #> GIMME Network Analysis #> ------------------------------  #> Subjects:   3  #> Variables:  4  ( V1, V2, V3, V4 ) #> AR paths:   yes  #> Hybrid:     no  #>  #> Group-level paths found: 0  #>  #> Individual-level paths:  mean 1.3, range 0-3 #>  #> Proportion of subjects with each path: #>  #>   Temporal [directed] #>     weights [0.333, 1.000]  |  +6 / -0 edges #>        V1 V2   V3   V4 #>     V1  1  0 0.00 0.00 #>     V2  0  1 0.33 0.33 #>     V3  0  0 1.00 0.00 #>     V4  0  0 0.00 1.00 #>  #>   Contemporaneous [directed] #>     weights [0.333, 0.333]  |  +2 / -0 edges #>        V1   V2 V3   V4 #>     V1  0 0.00  0 0.00 #>     V2  0 0.00  0 0.00 #>     V3  0 0.00  0 0.33 #>     V4  0 0.33  0 0.00 #>  #>   plot(x)  (faithful gimme-style mixed network) | plot(x, layer = "temporal")  #>   edges(x) | nodes(x) | summary(x) | coefs(x) | matrices(x) # }

title: Build a Multilevel Vector Autoregression (mlVAR) network — fit_mlvar
text: algorithm follows mlVAR's lmer pipeline exactly: Drop rows NA id/day/beep optionally grand-mean standardize variable. Expand per-(id, day) beep grid right-join original values, producing augmented panel (augData). Add within-person lagged predictors (L1_*) person-mean predictors (PM_*). outcome variable fit lmer(y ~ within + -except--PM + (1 | id)) REML = FALSE. Collect fixed-effect temporal matrix B, -effect matrix Gamma, random-intercept SDs (mu_SD), lmer residual SDs. Contemporaneous network: cor2pcor(D %*% cov2cor(cor(resid)) %*% D). -subjects network: cor2pcor(pseudoinverse(forcePositive(D (- Gamma)))). committed oracle matrix validates fixed temporal/contemporaneous lmer fits lags 1 1+2, preprocessing controls (scale, scaleWithin, compareToLags, trueMeans, position detrending), lag-1 estimator = "lm", temporal = "unique" fits across every supported contemporaneous structure. configurations carry narrower declaration available equivalence().

title: Build a Bayesian multilevel VAR network (Mplus DSEM-targeted) — fit_mlvar_bayes
text: Native, pure-R Bayesian estimator two-level VAR(1) statistically reproduces Mplus DSEM output (estimator behind mlVAR::mlVAR(estimator = "Mplus")) without needing Mplus installed. conjugate Gibbs sampler estimates fixed temporal matrix, within-person residual (contemporaneous) network, -person network, using latent mean centring Mplus's default priors. Point estimates posterior medians posterior SDs 95% credible intervals.

title: Build a Bayesian multilevel VAR network (Mplus DSEM-targeted) — fit_mlvar_bayes
code: fit_mlvar_bayes(   data,   vars,   id,   day = NULL,   beep = NULL,   lags = 1L,   temporal = c("fixed", "default", "random"),   contemporaneous = c("fixed", "default"),   residual = c("fixed", "random"),   scale = TRUE,   scaleWithin = FALSE,   tinterval = NULL,   impute = FALSE,   n_iter = 4000L,   n_burnin = NULL,   n_chains = 2L,   thin = 1L,   seed = NULL,   min_obs = NULL,   subject = NULL,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Build a Bayesian multilevel VAR network (Mplus DSEM-targeted) — fit_mlvar_bayes
text: data data.frame containing panel data. vars Character vector variable column names model (length >= 2). id Character string naming person-ID column. day Character string naming day/session column, NULL. beep Character string naming measurement-occasion column, NULL. NULL, row position within (id, day) block used. lags Integer lag order; 1 supported (matches Mplus DSEM defaults ). temporal Character. "fixed" (default) fits fixed temporal effects random intercepts (Mplus DSEM temporal = "fixed"). "random" fits full DSEM person-specific temporal matrices B_i full random-effect covariance (mu_i, vec(B_i)); temporal network reports posterior mean transition matrix attr(fit, "slope_sd") holds per-coefficient random-slope SDs. "random" needs subjects estimable random-effect covariance: least 2 * (p + p^2) + 1 subjects. contemporaneous Character. "fixed" implemented. residual Character. "fixed" (default) uses one shared population within-person residual covariance. "random" (temporal = "random") gives subject residual covariance Sigma_W_i via conjugate hierarchical inverse-Wishart (Sigma_W_i ~ IW(Lambda, p + 2), Lambda ~ Wishart), matching DSEM person-specific innovation variances; reported contemporaneous network population-average residual covariance. scale Logical. Global grand-mean/SD standardization variable fitting (Mplus/mlVAR scale = TRUE). Default TRUE. scaleWithin Logical. Additionally within-person scale variable. Default FALSE. tinterval Numeric NULL. supplied, beep treated continuous time variable binned onto regular grid width (Mplus TINTERVAL); integer bin becomes occasion index gap-aware lagging, multiple observations one (id, day, bin) slot collapsed first. Lagging gap-aware cases: lag-1 pairs formed consecutive occasions, missing occasions never create spurious lag pairs. Default NULL. impute Logical. TRUE (temporal = "random"), missing observations imputed within model MCMC iteration (data augmentation), rather dropped: person's series expanded full occasion grid every latent cell drawn Gaussian full conditional (outcome t predictor t+1), using vectorised even/odd (checkerboard) block sweep. matches Mplus / Stan / JAGS handle missing data removes listwise-deletion bias heavy missingness, extra computational cost. Default FALSE. n_iter Integer. Total MCMC iterations per chain. Default 4000. n_burnin Integer. Burn-iterations discarded per chain. Default n_iter / 2 (Mplus's first-half burn-convention). n_chains Integer. Number independent chains. Default 2. thin Integer. Keep every thin-th post-burn-draw. Default 1. seed Integer NULL. Base RNG seed (chain c uses seed + c). min_obs Integer NULL. Keep subjects least many observations fitting. subject Optional vector naming exact subject(s) analyse. verbose Logical. Emit progress messages. Default FALSE.

text: net_mlvar_bayes object (also inheriting net_mlvar), named list three netobjects (temporal, contemporaneous, ) posterior-summary attributes. coefs() returns tidy table estimate (posterior median), posterior_sd, ci_lower, ci_upper, p (one-tailed), significant (95% CI excludes 0). Posterior draws max Gelman-Rubin PSR kept attributes.

title: Build a Bayesian multilevel VAR network (Mplus DSEM-targeted) — fit_mlvar_bayes
text: sampler alternates five conjugate full-conditional draws per iteration: latent person means mu_i (Gaussian), fixed temporal matrix B (matrix-normal), within residual covariance Sigma_W (inverse-Wishart), grand mean alpha (Gaussian), covariance Sigma_B (inverse-Wishart). lagged predictor recentred current mu_i draw every iteration (latent mean centring). Data globally standardized first (matching mlVAR's scale = TRUE); first observation block used lag (condition--first). Validated statistical (Monte-Carlo-error) equivalence real Mplus 9 DSEM output standardized synthetic panels: posterior medians B, Sigma_W, Sigma_B agree Mplus well within posterior SD.

title: Build a Bayesian multilevel VAR network (Mplus DSEM-targeted) — fit_mlvar_bayes
code: # \donttest{ set.seed(1) n_id <- 10; n_t <- 40; vars <- c("A", "B") rows <- lapply(seq_len(n_id), function(i) {   y <- matrix(0, n_t, 2)   for (t in 2:n_t) y[t, ] <- c(0.3, 0.15) * y[t - 1, ] + rnorm(2)   data.frame(id = i, beep = seq_len(n_t), A = y[, 1], B = y[, 2]) }) d <- do.call(rbind, rows) fit <- fit_mlvar_bayes(d, vars = vars, id = "id", beep = "beep",                          n_iter = 500, seed = 1) print(fit) #> Bayesian mlVAR (Mplus DSEM-targeted, temporal = fixed): 10 subjects, 390 observations, 2 variables #>   MCMC: 2 chains x 500 iter (250 burn-in), 500 draws | max PSR = 1.023 #>   Temporal 95% CIs excluding 0: 2 / 4 #>  #>   Temporal [directed] #>     weights [-0.088, 0.252]  |  +2 / -2 edges #>           A     B #>     A  0.25 -0.09 #>     B -0.07  0.13 #>  #>   Contemporaneous [undirected] #>     weights [-0.003, -0.003]  |  +0 / -1 edges #>       A B #>     A 0 0 #>     B 0 0 #>  #>   Between [undirected] #>     weights [0.312, 0.312]  |  +1 / -0 edges #>          A    B #>     A 0.00 0.31 #>     B 0.31 0.00 #>  #>   coefs(x) posterior median/SD/CI | matrices(x) | edges(x) | summary(x) coefs(fit) #>   outcome predictor    estimate posterior_sd    ci_lower   ci_upper     p #> 1       A         A  0.25209120   0.05021821  0.15945833 0.34723692 0.000 #> 2       A         B -0.06643236   0.04845493 -0.16844721 0.01897108 0.086 #> 3       B         A -0.08835699   0.05652692 -0.20220844 0.02199014 0.062 #> 4       B         B  0.12768325   0.05189932  0.02778123 0.22516873 0.012 #>   significant #> 1        TRUE #> 2       FALSE #> 3       FALSE #> 4        TRUE # }

title: Certify a graphical-lasso solution from its optimality conditions — glasso_kkt
text: Returns largest violation graphical-lasso stationarity (KKT) conditions. objective strictly convex, value near zero certifies global optimum directly estimand, appeal reference solver. W = Theta^{-1} subgradient conditions diagonal, unpenalised: \(W_{ii} = S_{ii}\); diagonal, penalised: \(W_{ii} - S_{ii} = \rho_{ii}\); -diagonal \(\Theta_{ij} \neq 0\): \(W_{ij} - S_{ij} = \rho_{ij}\,\mathrm{sign}(\Theta_{ij})\); -diagonal \(\Theta_{ij} = 0\): \(|W_{ij} - S_{ij}| \le \rho_{ij}\).

Required x bare matrix. penalize_diagonal Logical, whether diagonal penalised. Required x bare matrix. zero Two-column matrix hard-constrained (row, col) index pairs, passed glasso_fit(). Taken fit x glasso_result. Constrained entries excluded check: hard-constrained edge inactive-edge inequality apply, equality constraint carries multiplier absorbs residual. Checking anyway reports optimal fits non-optimal. active_tol Magnitude -diagonal entry counts active. Default 1e-8.

what: idiographic: Person-Specific Statistics and Dynamic Networks — idiographic-package
title: idiographic: Person-Specific Statistics and Dynamic Networks — idiographic-package
text: Person-specific within-person analysis intensive longitudinal ESM panel data. statistical workflow includes person-level descriptions (describe_persons()), centring, decomposition, lagging (preprocess_panel()), scoped regression (fit_lm(), fit_glm()), machine learning (fit_ml()), within-effects (fit_within_between()), coefficient pooling (pool_coefs()), subgroup analysis (test_subgroups(), find_subgroups()), treatment effects (fit_effects()), heterogeneity (fit_heterogeneity()).

title: idiographic: Person-Specific Statistics and Dynamic Networks — idiographic-package
text: Dynamic-network methods include network preprocessing audits (preprocess()), edge-stability diagnostics (estimate_stability()), rolling forecast validation (validate_forecast()), ordinary graphical vector autoregression (fit_var(), fit_graphical_var()), multilevel Bayesian VAR (fit_mlvar(), fit_mlvar_bayes()), unified SEM (fit_usem()), GIMME (fit_gimme()). Use fit_idiographic() registry-driven dispatch direct fit_*() functions. Results provide tidy accessors, readable print methods, diagnostics, plots appropriate analytical level. equivalence() reports exact validation scope attached registered network methods.

text: Builds lag-1 design used fit_graphical_var() fit_var(), optionally detrends differences series, returns tidy diagnostics missingness, day-boundary drops, simple linear trends, AR(1) persistence, split-half mean/variance drift, ADF-style unit-root screen, zero-variance variables. makes modelling input explicit estimating VAR, graphical VAR, uSEM, GIMME, mlVAR models; detrend also cleans non-stationary series place flags can rechecked transformed data.

code: preprocess(   data,   vars,   id = NULL,   day = NULL,   beep = NULL,   scale = TRUE,   center_within = TRUE,   detrend = "none",   checks = c("trend", "high_ar", "unit_root", "mean_shift", "sd_shift", "zero_variance"),   delete_missings = TRUE,   min_obs = NULL,   subject = NULL,   trend_alpha = 0.05,   ar_threshold = 0.95,   mean_shift_threshold = 0.8,   sd_ratio_threshold = 2,   unit_root_t_cutoff = -2.86 )

title: Preprocess and audit idiographic time-series data — preprocess
text: data data.frame matrix columns variables optional id/day/beep columns. vars Character vector variable names. id Character. Name person-ID column, NULL single series. day Character. Name day/session column, NULL. beep Character. Name measurement-occasion column, NULL. scale Logical. Whether standardize variables lagging. Default TRUE. center_within Logical. Whether centre within person one id present. Default TRUE. detrend remove non-stationarity series lagging. Either single string applied every variable, named character vector giving per-variable method (unlisted variables left untouched, e.g. c(planning = "difference", value = "linear")). available methods : "none" Default; diagnose , transform nothing. "auto" Detrend subject-series flagged, leaving stationary ones untouched: differencing stochastic trend (unit root near-unit-root persistence) linearly detrending deterministic trend. "clean whoever needs " option – subsetting, one call everyone. Can set per variable . "linear" Replace series residuals within-person regression linear time index. "difference" First-difference series within id/day blocks. diagnostics returned design reflect detrended series, trend unit-root flags can rechecked cleaning. checks Character vector selecting stationarity checkups run: "trend", "high_ar", "unit_root", "mean_shift", "sd_shift", "zero_variance". Defaults . Deselecting check turns flag report, flag_stationarity_risk roll-, "auto" detrend decision, can screen care . delete_missings Logical. TRUE, $pairs contains complete current/lagged rows; FALSE, first rows blocks incomplete rows retained NA lags, matching .gvar_tsdata(). Default TRUE. min_obs Integer NULL. Keep subjects least many observations. subject Optional vector naming subject(s) preprocess. trend_alpha Numeric p-value cutoff trend flag. Default 0.05. ar_threshold Numeric absolute AR(1) cutoff high-persistence flag. Default 0.95. mean_shift_threshold Numeric absolute standardized split-half mean shift cutoff. Default 0.8. sd_ratio_threshold Numeric split-half SD ratio cutoff. Default 2. unit_root_t_cutoff Numeric cutoff ADF-style lag-level t-statistic. Values greater cutoff flagged unit-root risk. Default -2.86, common large-sample intercept-screening cutoff.

title: Prepare repeated-measures data for idiographic modelling — preprocess_panel
text: Person-centering (center = "person") subtracts person's mean, remains person varies around . transform separates within-person effect -person one: raw scores predictor can look strong high-scoring people also score high outcome, within single person nothing. Grand-centering (center = "grand") subtracts one overall mean remove confound. Person-scaling (scale = "person") divides person's standard deviation, putting people common footing differ much fluctuate. Lagging (lag) adds <var>_lag1-style columns, shifted within person time order, person's yesterday never leaks another person's today. Rows predecessor get NA; fitters drop . lag counts occasions, elapsed time. sampling irregular real hazard: "previous occasion" may twenty minutes back one row three days back next, lag-1 effect estimated across one quantity. Give lag_max_gap refuse stretched ones – lagged value whose actual gap exceeds becomes NA rather silently incomparable number. describe_persons() reports gap_median gap_max can see whether applies data choosing. Detrending (detrend) removes linear time trend, remains fluctuation around person's trajectory rather trajectory . Two people can rising steadily appear strongly correlated every variable purely time passing. Following usual experience-sampling convention trend removed significant (detrend_alpha = 0.05); set detrend_alpha = 1 remove unconditionally. detrend = "person" fits person's trend occasions – idiographic choice, default meaning detrending – "grand" fits single trend across everyone. Detrending preserves series' level: residuals mean added back, detrend removes slope stays independent center. Series fewer three usable occasions left alone. Decomposing (decompose = TRUE) keeps halves instead choosing one: appends <var>_within (deviation person's mean) <var>_between (mean), leaving original column untouched. input within-model needs – see fit_within_between(), split internally training rows . Person-centering decomposition alternatives, companions: centering throws half away, asking refused.

title: Prepare repeated-measures data for idiographic modelling — preprocess_panel
code: # Within-person variation only, plus yesterday's efficacy. prepped <- preprocess_panel(srl, id = "name", time = "day",                       vars = "efficacy:monitoring",                       center = "person", lag = 1) fit_lm(prepped, y = "effort", x = c("efficacy", "efficacy_lag1"),        id = "name", time = "day") #> Idiographic Fit #>   Method:      lm #>   Outcome:     effort (regression) #>   Predictors:  2 (efficacy, efficacy_lag1) #>   ID:          name #>   Scope:       pooled + individual #>   Models:      lm [native] #>   Subjects:    36 #>   Predictions: 2300 #>   Best RMSE:   19.3110 (individual/lm) #>   Use metrics(), predictions(), coefs(), compare()  # Keep both halves, so the two effects can be compared in one model. A # between-person column is constant inside a person, so it only belongs in a # pooled model -- or use fit_within_between(), which handles the split itself. split <- preprocess_panel(srl, id = "name", vars = c("efficacy", "planning"),                     decompose = TRUE) fit_lm(split, y = "effort", x = c("efficacy_within", "efficacy_between"),        id = "name", scope = "pooled") #> Idiographic Fit #>   Method:      lm #>   Outcome:     effort (regression) #>   Predictors:  2 (efficacy_within, efficacy_between) #>   ID:          name #>   Scope:       pooled #>   Models:      lm [native] #>   Subjects:    36 #>   Predictions: 1150 #>   Best RMSE:   21.9757 (pooled/lm) #>   Use metrics(), predictions(), coefs(), compare()

title: idiographic 0.4.0.9000
text: Folded idiostats analytical engine idiographic. package now covers person-level descriptions correlations, LM/GLM expanded ML, rolling-origin validation, within-effects, coefficient pooling shrinkage, subgroup existence/discovery/modelling, treatment effects, heterogeneity analysis alongside existing dynamic-network estimators. Added describe_persons(), correlate_persons(), variance_components(), fit_lm(), fit_glm(), fit_rolling(), fit_within_between(), pool_coefs(), shrink_coefs(), test_subgroups(), find_subgroups(), fit_subgroups(), fit_effects(), fit_heterogeneity() tidy accessors, views, diagnostics, plots. Added preprocess_panel() person/grand centring scaling, detrending, within-decomposition, lags never cross person boundaries. established preprocess() network audit remains unchanged. fit_ml() now supports interfaces. Existing outcome/predictors calls retain original idioml_result; consolidated y/x calls support pooled, subgroup, individual scopes, richer native optional model registries, tuning, diagnostics, rolling validation. Consolidated statistical results use idiographic_* primary class retaining idiostats_* compatibility class downstream migration. Added statistical workflow index 16 detailed, function-specific vignettes complete non-network analysis layer. vignette uses bundled data, prints tidy results, renders decision-focused figure, interprets observed output, states assumptions failure conditions, ends guidance method selection. fit_ml() vignette includes temporal validation, baselines, tuning, scope comparison, person-level errors, prediction trajectories, permutation importance. Redesigned statistical plotting around ranked dot plots, interval displays, binned calibration, direct labels, temporal trajectories, consistent colour-accessible styling. Plots now foreground uncertainty, reference values, person-level failures instead relying default bar charts.

title: idiographic 0.2.0
text: Made CRAN package offline-first: mandatory imports standard R packages, lme4, lavaan, plotting, external backends optional. Competitor-oracle tests real-panel corpus now run separate opt-validation/ lane excluded CRAN tarball. Added registry-backed fit_idiographic() front door, estimator discovery, method-specific equivalence() declarations, package-wide equivalence_table() argument--argument argument_coverage() ledgers, common tidy accessors. 17 registered methods 315 current public formals now executable evidence classification; new unassessed arguments fail closure test. Expanded direct-oracle testing across graphicalVAR option combinations, mlVAR multi-lag/preprocessing/unique-model configurations, bivariate plus three-variable GIMME standard, hybrid, VAR searches. GIMME evidence now also covers fit statistics, uneven panels, exogenous-variable dimensions, interacting correction/standardization controls. Tightened public argument validation engine-specific controls silently ignored. Closed remaining executable evidence cells: 12 supported lag-1 lmer mlVAR structure combinations, per-subject/missing-data graphicalVAR fits, GIMME 10.0 correction/stopping/standardization/cutoff/forced-path controls, standardized ML/MLR uSEM fits, Mplus wrapper forwarding/conversion, Bayesian burn-/thinning, positive random-residual recovery, parallel mlVAR, base-R linear/logistic idiographic-ML engine equality. Migrated 20-panel real ESM mlVAR validation corpus Dynalytics/psychaj work CRAN-excluded validation/ lane, self-contained raw inputs, mlVAR 0.7.3 frozen oracles, provenance hashes, explicit regression coverage missing IDs, irregular occasion gaps, degenerate -person networks. Duplicate observation keys now fail clearly instead producing row-order-dependent preprocessing. Uniform fit_* naming estimators (breaking). Every model-fitting verb now uses single fit_ prefix: fit_var(), fit_graphical_var(), fit_mlvar(), fit_rolling_var(), estimators. Short model nicknames passed compare_idiographic(), estimate_stability(), validate_forecast() (example, "var" "graphical_var") unchanged. New native Bayesian estimators statistically reproduce Mplus DSEM output without requiring Mplus: fit_mlvar_bayes() — two-level Bayesian VAR(1) latent mean centring. temporal = "fixed" statistically validated frozen Mplus DSEM fixed-temporal + random-intercept fixtures; temporal = "random" fits full DSEM person-specific temporal matrices random-effect covariance (reports random-slope SDs). fit_var_bayes() — single-level Bayesian VAR(1), unregularized Bayesian analogue fit_graphical_var(). Pure-R conjugate Gibbs sampler (hand-rolled inverse-Wishart draws; new dependencies). Posterior median / SD / 95% CI / one-tailed p, three networks (temporal, contemporaneous, ), Gelman-Rubin PSR diagnostic. Validated statistical (Monte-Carlo-error) equivalence real Mplus 9 output frozen ground-truth fixtures parity tests. Added fit_ml() idiographic supervised machine-learning: ordered within-person train/test splits, person-specific models, pooled baselines held-rows, regression/classification metrics, row-level predictions, coefficient extraction via coefs(). model names statistical/ML model (example, "ridge"), estimator names implementation/backend (default "native"). new dependencies: native models include mean/majority baselines, OLS/logistic, ridge, lasso, elastic net, PCR, LDA, Gaussian naive Bayes, kNN, one-split trees. fit_idiographic_ml() fit_individualized_ml() remain aliases.
